name: Domain Password Spray (kerbrute / CrackMapExec)
description: Spray a single common password against many domain user accounts to avoid lockouts. Uses Kerberos (kerbrute) for quiet spraying.

recommended.note: Authenticated AD enumeration with found creds

notes: Try: Welcome1, Password1, SeasonYear!, CompanyName1. Wait one full observation window between spray rounds.

defense.why_it_works: Password spraying tests one or a few common passwords against many domain accounts — the inverse of brute force. By staying at or below the lockout threshold across all accounts and waiting out the observation window, an attacker avoids triggering account lockouts. Common passwords (Winter2024!, Company@123, Welcome1) succeed against a significant percentage of users in most enterprises.
defense.prerequisites: Valid domain account list (from kerbrute enumeration or LDAP). Knowledge of the domain password policy (lockout threshold, observation window). kerbrute, CrackMapExec, or Rubeus for spray. Network access to DC (Kerberos port 88) or LDAP.
defense.impact: T1110.003 Brute Force: Password Spraying. Compromises valid domain credentials without cracking. One successful account leads to authenticated domain foothold for full AD enumeration, Kerberoasting, and lateral movement.
defense.detection:
Pattern of Event 4625 (failed logon) or 4771 (Kerberos pre-auth failed) across many different accounts from a single source IP. SIEM rule: >10 distinct accounts with failed auth from same IP in 5 minutes. MDI 'Password spray' detection alert. Unusual auth failure time distribution (single burst at low rate across many accounts). CrackMapExec default User-Agent in HTTP/SMB auth logs.
Hash-cracking tools (john, hashcat) running after credential dump + high CPU/GPU from unsigned binaries accessing password hash files (DET0105).
Sudden valid logins from previously-dumped accounts correlating with cracking timeline.
Offline cracking inferred from subsequent successful CLI/web auth to routers/switches from dumped accounts.
defense.artifacts: Event 4625 (failed NTLM logon) or 4771 (Kerberos failed pre-auth) across many accounts from single IP | MDI alert: 'Password spray attack' | SIEM: distributed failed auth pattern | Kerberos KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_FAILED burst across many cnames
defense.prevention:
Strong lockout policy (threshold 5, 30-min window). Fine-Grained Password Policy for DA accounts (threshold 3, admin unlock required). Azure AD Password Protection (blocks common passwords). MDI deployment with password spray detection. MFA enforced — sprayed password useless without second factor. Monitor Event 4625/4771 patterns in SIEM.
Multi-factor Authentication: Implement MFA especially on externally facing services.
Password Policies: Follow NIST SP 800-63b guidelines for minimum length and complexity.
defense.evasion: Stay strictly under lockout threshold (e.g., 4 attempts with 3 allowed). Wait full observation window between attempts (e.g., 35 minutes if window is 30). Use Kerberos spray (4771/Event 4768) instead of NTLM spray (4625) — different event IDs may not be correlated. Distribute spray across multiple source IPs.
defense.misconfiguration: No account lockout (LockoutThreshold = 0). Common passwords in use (Welcome1, Seasonal+Year patterns). No MFA. Azure AD Password Protection not deployed. No SIEM correlation of failed-auth patterns.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Domain policy with no lockout:
Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy
# LockoutThreshold : 0 — unlimited spray possible

# Common predictable passwords in enterprise:
# Welcome1, Winter2024!, Company@123, [CompanyName]1!, Season+Year

# No MFA enforcement:
# Users authenticate with password only — single factor
defense.secure_config:
# Account lockout policy:
Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -Identity corp.local -LockoutThreshold 5 -LockoutObservationWindow (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 30) -LockoutDuration (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 30)

# Azure AD Password Protection (blocks common passwords + custom banned list):
# AAD portal → Security → Authentication Methods → Password Protection
# → Enable on-premises: Yes  (deploys agent to DCs)
# → Custom banned passwords: [CompanyName], [Seasons], Welcome, Password

# SIEM rule:
# (EventID=4625 OR EventID=4771) FROM same_source_ip TO >10 distinct accounts IN 5min → ALERT

# MDI: 'Password spray attack' detection alert enabled by default
